skill.name: doc-coauthoring
skill.description: Guides users through a staged workflow for writing documentation, proposals, technical specs, and decision documents. It helps gather context, draft sections, refine edits, and test reader understanding.
skill.summary: Structured coauthoring workflow for documentation, specs, proposals, and reader testing.

content.user_title: Draft Better Documentation With Guided Coauthoring
content.value_statement: Complex documents often lose context, structure, and reader clarity. This skill guides staged drafting, refinement, and reader testing in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through context gathering before drafting starts.
Suggests section structures for documentation, proposals, specs, and decision documents.
Creates a markdown scaffold or artifact when supported by the host tool.
Drafts sections through clarifying questions, brainstorming, curation, and feedback.
Tests reader understanding with sub-agents or manual fresh Claude prompts.
Reviews completed documents for flow, contradictions, redundancy, and unclear assumptions.
limitations: Does not verify facts, links, or technical claims without sources or connected tools.
Requires connectors or pasted content to access team discussions and shared documents.
Can create or edit files only where the host tool permits file access.
Reader testing depends on sub-agent support or manual user testing.

use_cases.title: Write a Technical Spec
use_cases.description: Turn project context into a structured technical approach with clear tradeoffs, constraints, and review questions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Decision Document
use_cases.description: Capture options, rationale, stakeholder concerns, and expected impact before a decision review.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Documentation
use_cases.description: Review a draft for missing context, weak structure, contradictions, and reader confusion.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Doc
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a guided workflow from a rough idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a document about [topic]. Guide me through context gathering, structure, drafting, and review.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Specific Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Work on one section after the document structure exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me draft the [section name] section. Ask clarifying questions, suggest points to include, then write a concise draft.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a document that already has content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft for structure, clarity, assumptions, contradictions, and unnecessary detail. Suggest targeted edits section by section.

prompt_templates.title: Run Reader Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate whether the document works for new readers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Test this document as a fresh reader. Predict likely reader questions, identify ambiguous areas, and recommend fixes for gaps.

output_examples.input: I need a decision doc for choosing a database migration strategy.
output_examples.output: The skill first asks about audience, constraints, alternatives, timelines, and desired impact. It then proposes sections for context, options, recommendation, risks, rollout, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Here is my rough spec. It feels too long and unclear.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews the draft for flow, repeated ideas, missing assumptions, and unclear tradeoffs. It suggests focused edits instead of rewriting the full document.

output_examples.input: We finished the draft. I want to know if readers will understand it.
output_examples.output: The skill generates likely reader questions, tests the document with a fresh context when possible, and reports what readers may misunderstand.

best_practices: Provide the audience, desired impact, constraints, and any required template before drafting.
Work section by section so feedback can shape later sections.
Run reader testing before sharing the document broadly.
anti_patterns: Skipping context gathering when the document depends on unstated history.
Asking for a full rewrite when targeted section edits would preserve intent.
Treating reader testing as fact verification for external claims.

faq.question: What types of documents does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports technical specs, proposals, decision documents, RFCs, planning documents, and similar structured writing.

faq.question: Does it write the whole document at once?
faq.answer: No. It builds documents section by section so the user can refine structure, tone, and content.

faq.question: Can it use existing documents or team discussions?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user provides files, text, links, or approved connectors that the host tool can access.

faq.question: Does it check whether facts are true?
faq.answer: It can flag claims that need verification, but facts require user-provided sources or connected research tools.

faq.question: What is reader testing?
faq.answer: Reader testing checks whether a fresh reader can understand the document, answer likely questions, and spot unclear assumptions.

faq.question: Can I use it in Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can create or edit markdown files when the host tool supports file operations.
